q: We introduce StateHarness, a runtime framework that maintains evolving project state without updating model parameters.
r: EC5: a new runtime framework evaluated on existing benchmarks (RefactorBench, LHTB, ChainSWE) with no contribution to the evaluation method.

q: we present MemDev-Bench to evaluate how memory systems affect code agents over diverse repository histories.
r: Include: benchmark evaluating memory mechanisms (a context mechanism) with Claude Code agents, group (b).

q: we present Hierarchical Skill Evolution (HSE), which progressively distills procedural knowledge from coding trajectories through hierarchical evidence aggregation.
r: Include: skill libraries for coding agents (Pi, Claude Code) evaluated with and without skills, group (b), not narrowed by EC5/EC6.

q: We propose Skill Dreaming, a framework that continuously evolves repository-specific skills from pull request streams.
r: Include: repository-specific skills guiding coding agents, group (b).

q: a rule in the harness’s native instruction file raises joint success from 0/120 to 117/120.
r: Include: controlled trials of what coding agents follow, including written rules in instruction files, group (b).

q: We introduce MUSE, a memory management framework combining multi-level memory with selective runtime injection for scientific coding agents.
r: Include: memory mechanism for coding agents (group (b), not narrowed by EC6), though limited to scientific coding.

q: We test whether executable contracts enforced while the agent works reduce rule violations compared with the same rules in the prompt, retrieved as guidance, or checked only after generation.
r: Include: compares engineering rules enforced at runtime against rules as prompt or instruction text in controlled studies with repetitions, group (b).

q: we present Hedwig, a CLI coding agent that dynamically adjusts its autonomy level based on developer-agent interactions across sessions.
r: EC5: a new agent with a small walkthrough evaluation; adds nothing to the evaluation method and is not a context-file study.

q: we propose the Gatekeeper Protocol, a domain-agnostic framework that eschews ambiguous, conversational interaction and instead enforces a formal, state-synchronized communication layer between the agent and the system.
r: EC5: a new interaction protocol tested on three programming tasks; the comparison of context strategies serves to promote it, not the evaluation method.

q: we introduce ToM-SWE, a conceptual framework that integrates theory-of-mind (ToM) reasoning into software engineering agents.
r: EC5: a new agent architecture on SWE-bench-style tasks; the stateful benchmark supports the agent and the tasks are issue repair.
